'''Shrinivas Ramchandra Kulkarni''' (born 4 October 1956) is an [[Indian-Americans|Indian American]] astronomer.<ref name="Ajit">{{cite web | url=http://www.frontline.in/static/html/fl1822/18220860.htm |title= An accomplished observer |date = 2001 |last1=Kembhavi |first1=Ajit| website=Frontline}}</ref> He is a professor of astronomy and [[planetary science]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech),<ref name="GPS">{{cite web|url=http://www.gps.caltech.edu/content/shrinivas-r-shri-kulkarni|title=Shrinivas R. (Shri) Kulkarni|website=Caltech Geology and Planetary Science|accessdate=29 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517101648/http://www.gps.caltech.edu/content/shrinivas-r-shri-kulkarni|archive-date=17 May 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was the director of the Caltech Optical Observatory (COO), overseeing the [[Palomar Observatory|Palomar]] and [[Keck Telescope|Keck]] among other telescopes.<ref name="GPS" />

==Early life and education==
Shrinivas Ramchandra Kulkarni was born on 4 October 1956 in the small town of [[Kurundwad]] in [[Maharashtra]], into a Hindu family. His father, Dr. R. H. Kulkarni, was a surgeon based in [[Hubballi]] and his mother, Vimala Kulkarni, was a home-maker. He is one of four children and has three sisters, Sunanda Kulkarni, [[Sudha Murthy]] (educator, author, philanthropist and wife of one of the co-founders of [[Infosys]]) and Jaishree Deshpande (wife of [[Gururaj Deshpande]]).<ref name="SuRK"/><ref name="www"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.leadcampus.org/blog/daughters-indiawho-made-us-proud/|title= Two daughters who made India proud| website= www.leadcampus.org| accessdate = 29 March 2017|date= 9 March 2017}}</ref>

Kulkarni and his sisters grew up in Hubballi, [[Karnataka]], and received their schooling at local schools there.<ref name="Ajit" /><ref name ="SuRK">{{cite web|url=http://www.rguhs.ac.in/senatecorrections2012/teachrepview.php?tcode=285&ccode=M009|date = 2012|title = Karnataka Online Teachers Data Base| website=Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences Karnataka}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rediff.com/news/2003/aug/19spec.htm|title=A star called Kulkarni|website=rediff.com|date=19 August 2003}}</ref><ref name="www">{{cite web| url=http://www.outlookindia.com/article.aspx?216431/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331210720/http://www.outlookindia.com/magazine/story/what-went-wrong/216431 | url-status=dead | archive-date=31 March 2017 |title=What Went Wrong?| date = 15 July 2002| author=Kamala Bhatt}}</ref> He obtained his MS in applied physics from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]] in 1978 and his PhD from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1983.<ref name ="GPS" />

==Career==
In 1987, Kulkarni obtained a position as faculty at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name ="GPS" /> [[Astrophysics Data System|ADS]] shows that his papers cover following fields: (1) HI absorption studies of [[Milky Way|Milky Way Galaxy]], (2) [[pulsar]]s, [[millisecond pulsar]]s, and [[globular cluster]] pulsars, (3) [[brown dwarf]]s and other sub-stellar objects, (4) [[Soft gamma repeater|soft gamma-ray repeaters]], (5) [[gamma-ray burst]]s, and (6) optical transients.

Kulkarni started off his career as a radio astronomer. He studied the [[Milky Way Galaxy]] using HI absorption under the guidance of his advisor Carl Heiles, and observed its four arms.<ref>{{cite book| last1=Kulkarni |first1=Shrinivas R.|year= 1983 | title= Studies of galactica HI in 21-centimeter absorption (PhD Thesis: UC Berkeley)|location= Berkeley, California| bibcode = 1984PhDT.........4K}}</ref>

He discovered the first [[millisecond pulsar]] called [[PSR B1937+21]]<ref>{{Citation |last1=Backer |first1=D. C. |last2=Kulkarni |first2=S. R. |last3=Heiles |first3=C. |last4=Davis |first4=M. M. |last5=Goss |first5=W. M. |title=A millisecond pulsar |year=1982 |journal=Nature |volume=300 |issue=5893 |pages=615–618 |bibcode=1982Natur.300..615B |doi=10.1038/300615a0 |s2cid=4247734}}</ref> with [[Donald Backer]] and colleagues, while he was a graduate student. In 1986, he found the first optical counterpart of binary pulsars,<ref>{{Citation | journal = Astrophysical Journal|last=Kulkarni|first=S. R.|year=1986|title=Optical Identification of Binary Pulsars - Implication for Magnetic Field Decay in Neutron Stars|volume=306|pages=L85| bibcode = 1986ApJ...306L..85K|doi = 10.1086/184711 |url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/37479/1/1986ApJ___306L__85K.pdf}}</ref> while he was a Millikan Fellow at California Institute of Technology. He was instrumental in discovery of the first [[globular cluster]] pulsar in 1987<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Lyne |first1 = A. G. | last2 = Brinklow | first2 = A. | last3 = Middleditch | first3 = J. | last4 = Kulkarni | first4 = S. R. | last5 = Backer | first5 = D. C. | last6 = Clifton | first6 = T. R. | year = 1987 | title = The Discovery of a Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M28) | journal = Nature | volume = 328 |issue = 6129 | pages = 399–401 | bibcode = 1987Natur.328..399L|doi = 10.1038/328399a0 |s2cid = 4333586 }}</ref> using a supercomputer.

With [[Dale Frail]] at [[NRAO]] and Toshio Murakami and his colleagues at ISAS (predecessor of [[JAXA]] that was led by [[Yasuo Tanaka (astronomer)|Yasuo Tanaka]] at that time), Kulkarni showed that [[soft gamma repeaters|soft gamma-ray repeaters]] are [[neutron star]]s associated with [[supernova remnants]].<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Kulkarni | first1 = S. R. | last2 = Frail | first2 = D. A. | year = 1993 | title = Identification of a supernova remnant coincident with the soft gamma-ray repeater SGR 1806-20 | journal = Nature | volume = 365 | issue = 6441 | pages = 33–35 | bibcode = 1993Natur.365...33K|doi = 10.1038/365033a0 | s2cid = 4357312 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1 = Murakami | first1 = T. | last2 = Tanaka | first2 = Y. | last3 = Kulkarni | first3 = S. R. |display-authors=etal | year = 1994 | title = X-ray dentification of a supernova the soft gamma-ray repeater 1806-20 | journal = Nature | volume = 368 | issue = 6467 | pages = 127–129 | bibcode = 1994Natur.368..127M| doi = 10.1038/368127a0 | s2cid = 4350956 }}</ref> This discovery eventually led to the understanding that [[neutron star]]s with extremely high magnetic field called [[magnetar]]s are the [[soft gamma repeaters|soft gamma-ray repeaters]].<ref>{{citation| last1=Kulkarni | first1=S. R.|last2=Thompson |first2=Christopher|year=1998| journal=Nature| volume=393 | issue=6682|pages=215–216 |title=Neutron Stars: A star powered by magnetism | bibcode=1998Natur.393..215K|doi = 10.1038/30357 | s2cid=205000444}}</ref>

[[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]]-NRAO team which he led showed in 1997 that [[gamma-ray bursts]] came from extra-galactic sources,<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Metzgar | first1 = M. R. | last2 = Djorgovski | first2 = S. G. | last3 = Kulkarni | first3 = S. R. |display-authors=etal | year = 1997 | title = Spectral constraints on the redshift of the optical counterpart to the gamma-ray burst of 8 May 1997 | journal = Nature | volume = 387 | issue = 6636 | pages = 878–880 | bibcode = 1997Natur.387..878M|doi = 10.1038/43132 | doi-access = free }}</ref> and identified optical counterparts.<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Djorgovski | first1 = S. G. | last2 = Metzgar | first2 = M. R. | last3 = Kulkarni | first3 = S. R. |display-authors=etal  | year = 1997 | title = The optical counterpart to the gamma-ray burst GRB970508 | journal = Nature | volume = 387 | issue = 6636 | pages = 876–878 | bibcode = 1997Natur.387..876D|doi = 10.1038/43126 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Their research initiated the detailed studies of the sources of [[gamma-ray bursts]] along with the European team led by [[Jan van Paradijs]].

He was also a member of the Caltech team that observed the first irrefutable [[brown dwarf]] in 1994 that orbited around a star called [[Gliese 229]].<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Nakajima | first1 = T. | last2 = Oppenheimer | first2 = B. R. | last3 = Kulkarni | first3 = S. R. | last4 = Golimowski | first4 = D. A. | last5 = Matthews | first5 = K. | last6 = Durrance | first6 = S. | title = Discovery of a Cool Brown Dwarf | year = 1995 | journal = Nature | volume = 378 | issue = 6556 | pages = 463–465| bibcode = 1995Natur.378..463N|doi = 10.1038/378463a0 | s2cid = 4351772 }}</ref>

His recent work involved [[Palomar Transient Factory]] which has succeeded in identifying the new groups of optical transients such as [[superluminous supernova]]e,<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Quimby | first1 = R. M. | last2 = Kulkarni | first2 = S. R. | last3 = Kasliwal | first3 = M. M. |display-authors=etal | title = Hydrogen-poor super luminous stellar explosions | year = 2011 | journal = Nature | volume = 474 | issue = 7352 | pages = 487–489 | bibcode = 2011Natur.474..487Q|arxiv = 0910.0059 |doi = 10.1038/nature10095 | pmid = 21654747 | s2cid = 4333823 }}</ref> [[calcium-rich supernova]]e,<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Kasliwal | first1 = M. M. | last2 = Kulkarni | first2 = S. R. | last3 = Arcavi | first3 = I. |display-authors=etal | title = Calcium-Rich Transients in the Remote Outskerts of Galaxies | year = 2012 | journal = Astrophysical Journal| volume = 755 | issue = 2 | page = 161 | bibcode = 2012ApJ...755..161K|arxiv = 1111.6109 |doi = 10.1088/0004-637X/755/2/161 | s2cid = 32808402 }}</ref> and [[luminous red nova]]e.<ref>{{Citation | last1 = Rau | first1 = A. | last2 = Kulkarni | first2 = S. R. | last3 = Ofek | first3 = E. O. | last4 = Yan | first4 = L. | title = Spitzer Observations of the New Luminous Red Nova M85 OT2006-1 | year = 2007 | journal = Astrophysical Journal | volume = 659 | issue = 2 | pages = 1536–1540 | bibcode = 2007ApJ...659.1536R | doi=10.1086/512672| arxiv = astro-ph/0612161 | s2cid = 8913778 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1 = Kasliwal | first1 = M. M. | last2 = Kulkarni | first2 = S. R. | last3 = Arcavi | first3 = I. |display-authors=etal | title = PTF 10fqs: A Luminous Red Nova in the Spiral Galaxy Messier 99 | year = 2011 | journal = Nature | volume = 730 | issue = 2 | pages = 134 | bibcode = 2012ApJ...755..161K|arxiv = 1111.6109 |doi = 10.1088/0004-637X/755/2/161 | s2cid = 32808402 }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Some of the awards he has received include the following: 

* NSF's [[Alan T. Waterman Award]] in 1992<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/od/waterman/waterman_recipients.jsp#1992|title=Alan T. Waterman Award Recipients, 1976 - present|website=American Astronomical Society|access-date=29 November 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150302020546/http://www.nsf.gov/od/waterman/waterman_recipients.jsp#1992|archivedate=2 March 2015}}</ref> 
* [[Helen B. Warner Prize]] from the [[American Astronomical Society]] in 1991<ref>{{Citation | title = Shrinivas Kulkarni received the 1991 Helen B. Warner Prize of the American Astronomical Society. | year = 1991 | journal = Physics Today | volume = 44 | issue = 6 | pages = f129| bibcode = 1991PhT....44f.129. | doi=10.1063/1.2810153}}</ref> 
* Jansky Prize in 2002<ref>{{cite web|url=https://science.nrao.edu/science/jansky-lecture|title=Jansky Lectureship |website =science.nrao.edu|date=24 August 2016}}</ref> 
* Dan David Prize in 2017<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.caltech.edu/news/caltech-astronomer-receives-2017-dan-david-prize-54104 | website=www.caltech.edu|date=10 February 2017 | title=Caltech Astronomer Receives 2017 Dan David Prize}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dandavidprize.org/laureates/2017|accessdate=27 March 2017|title=Laureates 2017|website= www.dandavidprize.org}}</ref> 
* [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society]] in 2026 <ref>[https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2026-01/Gold%20Medal%20%28A%29%20-%20Professor%20Shrinivas%20Kulkarni.pdf]</ref>

In 2015, he received an [[honorary doctorate]] from [[Radboud University]] in the [[Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.ru.nl/english/news-agenda/news/vm/2015/april/kulkarni-2015/ |title=Honorary Doctorate for astronomer Shrinivas Kulkarni |accessdate=2 June 2017}}</ref> In 2024, he was awarded the [[Shaw Prize]] in Astronomy.<ref name=shaw>{{cite web|url=https://www.shawprize.org/laureates/2024-astronomy/|website=shawprize.org|title=The Shaw Prize in Astronomy 2024}}</ref><ref name=shaw2>{{cite web|url=https://www.shawprize.org/news/announcement-press-conference-2024-press-release|website=shawprize.org|title= Shaw Prize 2024}}</ref>

==Services to the field==
Kulkarni has been the Jury Chair for the [[Infosys Prize]] for the discipline of [[Physical Sciences]] since 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/2009/index.asp |title=Jury Chairs 2009 |website=Infosys Science Foundation |accessdate=29 March 2017 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328200156/http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/2009/index.asp |archivedate=28 March 2017 }}</ref> The prize is awarded by the Infosys Foundation, whose founder is Kulkarni's brother-in-law, [[N. R. Narayana Murthy|Narayana Murthy]].

Kulkarni is a member of four national academies. He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]], London, in 2001,<ref name="FRS" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://rediff.com/2001/may/31us3.htm|title=The Royal Society inducts Shrinivas Kulkarni|website=rediff.com|date=2001}}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences|United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2003,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/shrinivas-r-kulkarni-lklng6/ |title=Member Directory|website = National Academy of Science, US | access-date= 25 March 2017}}</ref> an honorary fellow of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 2012,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ias.ac.in/listing/fellows/honorary | title=Honorary Fellows| website= Indian Academy of Science|accessdate= 25 March 2017}}</ref> and a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] on 12 September 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/actueel/nieuws/knaw-kiest-zestien-nieuwe-leden-2016 |title=KNAW kiest zestien nieuwe leden |language=Dutch |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |accessdate=25 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/15091 |title=Shrnivas Kulkarni |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |accessdate= 25 March 2017}}</ref>
